reason: The DNA building blocks match positions alongside existing DNA, so they seem useful for copying the cell's instructions.
expectation: The cell will use the building blocks to copy its DNA.

alternatives.reason: The fats could also help make the extra membrane.

effect: The cell has copied its DNA; making extra membrane is the remaining visible goal.
reaction: The picture helps me see that each old DNA strand pairs with a new one.
reason: The membrane fats are the visible material for making extra membrane in the growing cell.
expectation: The cell will use the fats to make extra membrane.

effect: The new membrane is ready in sacs but has not yet joined the cell boundary; division is now the goal.
reaction: I hadn't expected the new membrane to be stored in sacs first.
reason: The membrane supply is ready to join the cell, which should help it divide.
expectation: The membrane will join the cell and help it finish dividing into two cells with DNA copies.

effect: The membrane joined the growing cell, and the copied chromosomes separated so each daughter cell received a complete set. The repeated sequence explains the resulting cell population.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the membrane supply and DNA copies come together in one division sequence.

mostWorthwhile.text: Finishing division was most worthwhile because the sequence connected cell growth, chromosome separation and the two resulting cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the membrane supply felt less informative on its own; the picture showed sacs forming but did not explain much about the membrane-making structures.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the new membrane first appeared in sacs rather than immediately enlarging the cell boundary.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the membrane-making structures were not explained in detail.

continue.text: I would continue to see what the unspecialized cells become; division produced a population, but it has not yet shown what those cells will do.
